Ghim's tee shot drifted left into the rough on the sharp dogleg right hole, avoiding the water but landing in a bad spot. His approach shot fell short and right, burying itself in lush rough that made contact difficult. He hacked out, missed the green with his fourth shot, and two putts later the damage was done. The result was a T-6 finish that left him with a sour taste in his mouth and a lighter wallet.
